thread_analysis.thread_summary: Panasonic Connect (contact Taku Takada, GSOL division) works with Allion (Masaya Iida, with technical answers drafted by Itsuo Sakai) on Bluetooth certification scoping for a set-top box (STB) sharing a Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip, while the target SoC is still in development and tested via a prior-generation prototype. The thread covers feature-capping/certification-scope strategy (whether unadvertised, pre-certified, or future features need testing), detailed ICS terminology clarification for two specific profile items, and an internal billing-policy decision about charging for detailed product-specification advice.
all_questions_found: Can a working-but-unadvertised feature (A2DP) skip certification, and is there an alternative to SDP/GATT UUID capping? (see thread_0230_case_01)
Does capping already chip/module-certified but unused profiles require retesting? (see thread_0230_case_02)
Should an uncertain future feature (LE Audio) be certified upfront, and how costly/difficult is adding it later? (see thread_0230_case_03)
What do 'Bluetooth Network Encapsulation Protocol' (PAN) and 'HOGP-Host role' / Scan Parameters Profile dependency actually mean, with STB examples? (see thread_0230_case_04)
(Internal) Should detailed product-specification applicability review be billed separately from certification support? (see thread_0230_case_05)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Certification scope tracks actual functional capability (not marketing claims), with SDP/GATT UUID de-registration as the only verified compliant way to exempt a feature; profiles already certified at chip/module level don't need retesting when capped at the product level; deferring an uncertain future feature only costs a new registration fee later, not added technical difficulty; and specific ICS cross-dependencies (Scan Parameters Profile required for either HOGP Host role) needed plain-language translation since they aren't well-documented externally. A parallel internal discussion distinguished certification-process questions (Allion's responsibility) from product-design-decision questions (customer's responsibility), deciding the latter should be given as free reference opinions when discussed in this kind of advisory context.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Across the technical questions, the unifying principle is that certification obligations are driven by objective functional/protocol facts (does the feature run, is it already certified upstream, what does the ICS dependency actually require) rather than marketing intent or assumption; the internal billing question applied a parallel responsibility-based principle (process answers vs. design-decision opinions).
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: See the individual case files (thread_0230_case_01 through thread_0230_case_05) for specific risks of each question.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — Allion's answers consistently separated what it could answer with full responsibility (certification process and ICS mechanics) from what remained the customer's own design decision, and applied that distinction transparently to the billing question as well.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: For STB/consumer-electronics customers navigating multi-profile certification scoping with chip vendors still mid-development, proactively distinguish protocol-level facts (functional capability, chip/module-level pre-certification, ICS dependencies) from business/design decisions (whether to certify now vs. later, whether a feature should exist at all), and apply that same distinction internally when deciding whether detailed advisory work should be billed.
